about: Unicode text -> Shree-Lipi 7 Punjabi (Gurmukhi) bytes (fonts SHREE-PUN7-0951/0952 = WPUN7001/2.TTF; the 4/5/6 fonts SHREE-PUN-0950/0951/0952/0955/0956 = S09xx0F2.TTF draw the same bytes, except ₹ 3C which they lack), answered by Shree's own composers S8PunU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Pun764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, raw bytes) for the same keystroke. bytes = the 7 composer's raw output, one hex byte per glyph code. Every probe set and every vendor keyboard was captured twice in separate processes: byte-identical. kind: vendor-key = a key (layer 0, Ctrl+Space, or the composer raw code layer) of one of the 12 shipped .PUN keyboards loaded from its ORIGINAL path (the composers switch typing mode by name: ENG/NEWROMA/PHONETIC/ROMA are phonetic, a bindi key types tippi there); source names the keyboard, key and codes. canonical = probe in Shree's typing order for Gurmukhi: the i-sign ਿ (code 67) struck FIRST, every other sign after the letter, bindi/tippi/visarga/addak after the sign, subjoined ੍ਰ ੍ਹ ੍ਵ ੍ਯ with their own codes D1 D2 D0 4C, nukta letters = letter + nukta D7 (the 7 composer writes one glyph: ਸ਼ 66 ਖ਼ 69 ਗ਼ 6A ਜ਼ 6B ਫ਼ 6C ਲ਼ B4); canonical:halant = a virama typed with the halant code 44 (visible B5); canonical:link / pending-link = a virama typed with the link code 64, for which the 7 composer writes NO glyph (ਕ੍ਤ = 48 57, the same bytes as ਕਤ); canonical:tippi-typed-written-as-bindi and canonical:addak+bindi-written-as-adak-bindi = the composers' own spelling rules (accepted); canonical:ੴ = the vendor slot 31 51 (੧ + onkar arc B0). preferred: for a virama that is not a subjoined form, the halant (B5) spelling - a choice, since the composer writes both: Unicode fonts draw ੍ visibly there and B5 reads back as ੍, the link spelling reads back as two plain letters; accepted keeps both. For C੍ਰ C੍ਹ C੍ਵ C੍ਯ only the subjoined spelling is accepted (6E for ਕ੍ਰ, else C 6F / C AA / C AB / C 62). alt:* = the composer answer for another typing order or a visibly different form (ਿ struck after the letter, a sign struck before the subjoined code or a mark before the sign, C + link/halant + ਰ ਹ ਵ ਯ = two full letters instead of the subjoined form, ੴ as code 51 alone = B0 without the ੧) - kept, not used as truth. quirk:* = the Unicode composer wrote something other than the codes mean (ਡ + nukta -> ੜ, ੳ ੰ written ੳਂ with the 7 composer losing it, ਓ + ੁ -> ਉ), or the 7 composer dropped a code the Unicode composer wrote (“ ” ॥ ੴ(E0) ਇ(E4) alone: nothing; the nukta on letters with no nukta glyph; the addak when ਂ follows it after ੀ ੇ ੈ ੌ; a subjoined code / bindi / tippi struck after a late i-sign), or answered on carrier byte 07 - kept for evidence, not used. The two codes only the legacy composer types (U answers nothing): 41 -> 40 (an avagraha-like ऽ glyph) and EE -> A9 (a short low dash); they are not in the truth. Unicode keys are what the Unicode composer wrote (nukta letters come back precomposed U+0A33 U+0A36 U+0A59-U+0A5B U+0A5E, which NFC decomposes - a table needs both forms), except that ੲ/ੳ/ਅ + sign are filed under the independent vowel the composer writes. Rules with examples: pun7-patterns.txt.

fontCheck.method: fonts/family-check.json (fontcmp.js): (3,1) cmap of WPUN7001.TTF (SHREE-PUN7-0951), WPUN7002.TTF (SHREE-PUN7-0952), S09500F2/S09510F2/S09520F2/S09550F2/S09560F2.TTF (SHREE-PUN-0950/0951/0952/0955/0956); per code glyph id, advance, sha1 of the glyf bytes; same-design pairs 0951 and 0952 compared outline by outline; every code of every face drawn by glyph index in fonts/codes-*.png.
fontCheck.result: Same design (0951: WPUN7001 vs S09510F2; 0952: WPUN7002 vs S09520F2): 118 of 119 codes identical in outline bytes and advance; the only difference is 3C (₹), present in the two 7 faces only. All five 4/5/6 faces map the same 118 codes to the same glyph ids, and both 7 faces the same 119 codes. ONE table serves both families; for a 4/5/6 face ₹ (3C) has no glyph.

counts.notProbed: Sequences longer than 4 codes cannot be typed with one key (a conjunct slot holds at most 4 codes), so: a two-consonant cluster with the i-sign AND a tail (ਿ C੍C ੰ), C੍C + subjoined + a vowel sign, a nukta letter (2 codes) in a cluster with a vowel sign, and three-consonant clusters other than C੍C + ੍ਰ/੍ਹ/੍ਵ/੍ਯ are not in the truth. Udaat ੑ (U+0A51), yakash ੵ (U+0A75), ੶ and the Gurmukhi abbreviation sign have no code: no key of any Shree keyboard and no code 21-FE gives them.
